scenarios.title: Search a possible base system next to the strike force
scenarios.goal: Find the hidden Rebel base. The strike force at Naboo (searched last round, not pinned now) can reach three unsearched systems that are still possible base locations; activating one of them and moving ground units in searches it this turn. Activations that only bring ground closer to other possible locations search nothing yet; passing wastes the leaders of the round.

scenarios.title: Bring ground units into the activated system, not ships only
scenarios.goal: The Empire activated an unsearched system and wants it searched. Only Imperial ground units reveal the base; they need a Star Destroyer to carry them. Moving the ground in (with or without the TIE fighters) searches the system when the activation ends; moving the ship alone or finishing now leaves it unsearched.

scenarios.title: The Death Star alone does not search a system
scenarios.goal: The Empire activated an unsearched system and moved only the Death Star in; the troops it could have carried stayed behind without transport. Ships, the Death Star included, never reveal the base, so the system is not searched yet: ground units must still come in from the other neighbour before the activation is finished.

scenarios.title: Finish the activation once the ground is in
scenarios.goal: Imperial ground units already moved into the activated, unsearched system. The search happens when the movement of the activation is over, so finishing now completes it. One more troop move is harmless but adds nothing; moving an empty carrier in strands the stormtrooper it would have carried.

scenarios.title: Do not lock your own forces with a leader
scenarios.goal: Vader stays at Naboo until the Refresh Phase, so the strike force there cannot move this round. Keep hunting with forces that can still move: activate an unsearched system without Imperial units that ground can reach. Activating a system that already holds Imperial ground searches nothing (the base would already be revealed there) and pins those units too; passing wastes the remaining leaders.

scenarios.title: Activate the revealed, abandoned base
scenarios.goal: The base is revealed and no Rebel unit is left in it; Imperial units stand next to it. Activating the base system lets them move in, and the Empire wins as soon as one Imperial unit is there with no Rebel unit. Any other activation or a pass gives the Rebels a turn to move units back in.

scenarios.title: Move any unit into the empty revealed base
scenarios.goal: The Empire activated the revealed base that holds no Rebel unit. Any Imperial unit moving in wins the game at once: a ship is enough here, because the base is already revealed. Finishing without a move throws the win away.

scenarios.title: Keep hunting after the Rebels passed
scenarios.goal: The Rebels passed for the round. If the Empire passes too, the Command Phase ends at once and time advances towards the Rebel victory, while all four Imperial leaders are still unused. No possible base location is in reach yet, so the useful turn is to activate a system that brings ground next to possible locations.

scenarios.title: Keep a unit in the revealed base
scenarios.goal: The base is revealed and Imperial ground units stand in it. The Empire wins the moment no Rebel unit is left there, so carrying the whole garrison out loses at once. Finishing (or moving the fleet from Bothawui) keeps the base held; moving part of the garrison out still leaves it held but weaker.

scenarios.title: Do not empty the hidden base under threat
scenarios.goal: Imperial ground units stand next to the hidden base and can move in on the next Imperial turn. Their arrival reveals the base; if no Rebel unit is in it then, the Empire wins at once. Keep the garrison home: finish or move the fleet from Bothawui. Moving part of the garrison out keeps the base held but weaker.

scenarios.title: Reoccupy the empty base before the Empire arrives
scenarios.goal: The hidden base is empty and unpinned Imperial ground stands next to it: if it moves in, the base is revealed with no Rebel unit and the Empire wins. The evacuated garrison cannot come back this round (Dodonna pins Tatooine), but the fleet at Bothawui can: activate the base now. Passing or activating elsewhere leaves the base open.

scenarios.title: Move units back into the empty base
scenarios.goal: The Rebels activated their empty hidden base while Imperial ground stands next to it. Any Rebel unit moved in keeps the Empire from winning when it arrives; the fleet at Bothawui can carry troops (the evacuated garrison at Tatooine is pinned by its leader). Finishing without a move leaves the base empty.

scenarios.title: Last round: passing is fine
scenarios.goal: Time is one space short of reputation and the base is hidden and guarded. When both sides pass, time advances and the Rebels win. Passing ends the Rebel part of the round with no risk; activating a system elsewhere is harmless; activating the base itself only shows the Empire where it is.

scenarios.title: Finish when no move helps
scenarios.goal: The Rebels activated a system next to their hidden base; the only units that could move in are the base garrison. No Imperial force is near, so moving it out gains nothing: finish the activation. Moving part of the garrison keeps the base held; carrying all of it out leaves the base empty for the first Imperial search.
